name: The Gibeonites, and Israel’s oath
charge: Obtaining a covenant by fraud; and Israel making it without asking counsel at the mouth of the Lord
summary: The Hivites of Gibeon, Hamites of the land Israel was commanded to destroy, came to Gilgal in old sacks, rent wine bottles and mouldy bread, leaning on the fame of the Most High and claiming to come from a far country. They knew Israel’s own law of war, and they built the lie on it. The men of Israel were suspicious, asked the right questions, and then took of their victuals and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord. That one omission became a snare to the nation for centuries. The princes held the oath, and the Gibeonites were cursed to be hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God.
offenseFull: When the kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, Hamites better known as Nilotic Africans, gathered to fight Joshua and Israel with one accord, the inhabitants of Gibeon worked wilily: they made as if they had been ambassadors, with old sacks on their asses, old wine bottles rent and bound up, old clouted shoes, old garments, and bread dry and mouldy (Joshua 9:1-5). Israel was commanded to destroy all the inhabitants of the land, the very nations listed in the first verse, so their only hope was to pretend they were not of them. And the lie was built on Israel’s own law of war: a city very far off was to be offered peace first, and if it answered peace its people became tributaries and served Israel, while the cities of these nations were to be utterly destroyed (Deuteronomy 20:10-15, 16-17). They knew the rule, so they claimed the far country and asked for a league (Joshua 9:6).

They leaned on the fame of the Most High to sell it, saying they had come because of the name of the Lord Israel’s God, having heard all He did in Egypt and to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan beyond Jordan (Joshua 9:9-10). The props sold the story. The men of Israel were suspicious at first, saying the strangers might dwell among them, and Joshua pressed them on who they were and where they came from (Joshua 9:7-8). Israel’s fault is set down in one clause: the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord (Joshua 9:14-15). The Most High says let reason go before every enterprise and counsel before every action (Ecclesiasticus 37:16); they reasoned it out among themselves instead of inquiring. The league forbidden with the inhabitants of the land (Exodus 23:32; Deuteronomy 7:2) was made through not asking, and it became a snare to the nation for centuries after.
judgmentFull: At the end of three days Israel heard that they were their neighbours and dwelt among them, and the children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn to them by the Lord God of Israel; all the congregation murmured against the princes, but the princes held the line: they had sworn by the Lord God of Israel and could not touch them, and would let them live, so that wrath would not be on them because of the oath (Joshua 9:16-21). Our fathers were wrong in one situation, but they were upright men in holding to their word: when a man vows a vow to God, he is not to defer to pay it, for it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay (Ecclesiastes 5:4-6). A vow made before the Most High stands, even one gotten by guile.

Joshua called for them, asked why they had beguiled him by saying they were very far off when they dwelt among them, and pronounced them cursed: none of them would be freed from being bondmen, hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of his God (Joshua 9:22-23). Hewers of wood and drawers of water means servants, according to the law of the Most High pertaining to the other nations: the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel are to be of the heathen round about, taken as an inheritance for the children after them, while over their own brethren the children of Israel were not to rule with rigour (Leviticus 25:44-46). There was no equality among the nations then and there is none now; they were made for a purpose, and the reason they are not in it today is that Israel sinned and failed. The

Gibeonites themselves answered honestly that it had been told them how the Lord commanded Moses to give Israel all the land and to destroy all its inhabitants, so they were sore afraid of their lives, and Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the Lord (Joshua 9:24-27).

The oath bound Israel harder than it bound Gibeon: when Saul broke it, the Lord sent three years of famine in David’s day for Saul and his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites (2 Samuel 21:1), entered under Rizpah. The same ordeal plays out again when Christ returns: the sons of strangers will build up Israel’s walls and their kings will minister to her, and the nation and kingdom that will not serve her will perish and be utterly wasted (Isaiah 60:10-12), for to the man who overcomes and keeps His works to the end He gives power over the nations (Revelation 2:26). There is nothing new under the sun.

lawsResolved.text: Alliances and covenants (treaties) with pagan or ungodly nations are forbidden.
We should inquire of the LORD as the whether or not we are to go to battle with another nation.
If a man makes a vow to God or swears an oath to bind himself by contract or binding obligation, he shall not violate his word but shall do all that he stated.
You shall make no false or deceitful oath or covenant.
You shall not deal falsely or treacherously with your brethren.

text.text: And it came to pass, when all the kings which were on this side Jordan, in the hills, and in the valleys, and in all the coasts of the great sea over against Lebanon, the Hittite, and the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard thereof;
That they gathered themselves together, to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord.
And when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done unto Jericho and to Ai,
They did work wilily, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks upon their asses, and wine bottles, old, and rent, and bound up;
And old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy.
When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it.
And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.
And if it will make no peace with thee, but will make war against thee, then thou shalt besiege it:
And when the Lord thy God hath delivered it into thine hands, thou shalt smite every male thereof with the edge of the sword:

But the women, and the little ones, and the cattle, and all that is in the city, even all the spoil thereof, shalt thou take unto thyself; and thou shalt eat the spoil of thine enemies, which the Lord thy God hath given thee.
Thus shalt thou do unto all the cities which are very far off from thee, which are not of the cities of these nations.
But of the cities of these people, which the Lord thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth:
But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee:
And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us.
And they said unto him, From a very far country thy servants are come because of the name of the Lord thy God: for we have heard the fame of him, and all that he did in Egypt,
And all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites, that were beyond Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon, and to Og king of Bashan, which was at Ashtaroth.
And the men of Israel said unto the Hivites, Peradventure ye dwell among us; and how shall we make a league with you?
And they said unto Joshua, We are thy servants. And Joshua said unto them, Who are ye? and from whence come ye?
And the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord.
And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them.
Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.
Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
And when the Lord thy God shall deliver them before thee; thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them:
And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a league with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours, and that they dwelt among them.
And the children of Israel journeyed, and came unto their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Gibeon, and Chephirah, and Beeroth, and Kirjath–jearim.
And the children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn unto them by the Lord God of Israel. And all the congregation murmured against the princes.
But all the princes said unto all the congregation, We have sworn unto them by the Lord God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.
This we will do to them; we will even let them live, lest wrath be upon us, because of the oath which we sware unto them.
And the princes said unto them, Let them live; but let them be hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation; as the princes had promised them.
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
And Joshua called for them, and he spake unto them, saying, Wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you; when ye dwell among us?
Now therefore ye are cursed, and there shall none of you be freed from being bondmen, and hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God.
Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.
Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.

And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

And they answered Joshua, and said, Because it was certainly told thy servants, how that the Lord thy God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you, therefore we were sore afraid of our lives because of you, and have done this thing.
And now, behold, we are in thine hand: as it seemeth good and right unto thee to do unto us, do.
And so did he unto them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, that they slew them not.
And Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation, and for the altar of the Lord, even unto this day, in the place which he should choose.

Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the Lord. And the Lord answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.
And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.
Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.
For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.
And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations:
And when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done unto Jericho and to Ai,
They did work wilily, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks upon their asses, and wine bottles, old, and rent, and bound up;
And old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy.
And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us.
And the children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn unto them by the Lord God of Israel. And all the congregation murmured against the princes.
But all the princes said unto all the congregation, We have sworn unto them by the Lord God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.
This we will do to them; we will even let them live, lest wrath be upon us, because of the oath which we sware unto them.
And the princes said unto them, Let them live; but let them be hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation; as the princes had promised them.
